definition: A number represents a quantity or mathematical value.
An integer is a whole number that can be positive, negative, or zero.
Natural numbers are commonly the positive whole numbers, although conventions differ about including zero.
A rational number can be written as a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator.
An irrational number cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers.
Real numbers include rational and irrational numbers and can be represented on the number line.
A complex number has the form a + bi, where i² = -1.
Addition combines quantities. It is commonly represented with the + operator.
Subtraction finds the difference between quantities.
Multiplication represents repeated addition or scaling.
Division determines how one quantity is distributed or how many times one quantity fits into another.
A fraction represents a quantity using a numerator and denominator.
The numerator is the top part of a fraction.
The denominator is the bottom part of a fraction and cannot be zero.
A decimal represents a number using place values based on powers of ten.
A percentage represents a quantity out of 100.
A ratio compares quantities.
A proportion states that two ratios are equal.
Order of operations determines how mathematical expressions are evaluated, including parentheses, exponents, multiplication/division, and addition/subtraction.
A variable is a symbol representing a value that can change or an unknown value.
A constant is a value that does not change within a given mathematical context.
A mathematical expression combines values, variables, and operators.
An equation states that two expressions are equal.
An inequality compares quantities using symbols such as <, >, ≤, or ≥.
A linear equation has variables raised only to the first power.
A quadratic equation commonly has the form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.
A polynomial is an expression formed from variables and coefficients using non-negative integer powers.
A factor is a quantity that divides another quantity exactly.
A multiple is the result of multiplying a number by an integer.
A prime number greater than 1 has exactly two positive divisors: 1 and itself.
A composite number greater than 1 has more than two positive divisors.
The greatest common divisor is the largest positive integer that divides two or more integers.
The least common multiple is the smallest positive integer that is a multiple of two or more integers.
Modulo gives the remainder after integer division.
An exponent indicates repeated multiplication of a base.
A square root of x is a number whose square equals x.
A logarithm determines the exponent required to produce a number from a given base.
A function maps each allowed input to exactly one output.
The domain of a function is the set of allowed inputs.
The range of a function is the set of outputs it produces.
A coordinate identifies a position using an ordered set of values.
Slope measures the rate at which one quantity changes relative to another.
A vector has magnitude and direction.
A matrix is a rectangular arrangement of numbers or other values.
A set is a collection of distinct objects considered as a whole.
The union of sets contains elements belonging to at least one of the sets.
The intersection of sets contains elements common to all of the sets.
Probability measures how likely an event is, commonly from 0 to 1.
The arithmetic mean is the sum of values divided by the number of values.
The median is the middle value after ordered data is considered.
The mode is the value occurring most frequently in a dataset.
Variance measures the average squared deviation from the mean.
Standard deviation measures the typical spread of values around the mean.
A limit describes the value a function or sequence approaches.
A derivative measures the instantaneous rate of change of a function.
An integral represents accumulation and can be used to find areas and antiderivatives.
Calculus studies change, limits, derivatives, integrals, and accumulation.
Trigonometry studies relationships between angles and sides, especially in triangles.
Sine is a trigonometric function relating an angle to a ratio of sides.
Cosine is a trigonometric function relating an angle to a ratio of sides.
Tangent is a trigonometric function equal to sine divided by cosine where defined.
Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter and is approximately 3.14159.
Perimeter is the total distance around a two-dimensional shape.
Area measures the amount of two-dimensional space inside a boundary.
Volume measures the amount of three-dimensional space occupied by an object.
Geometry studies shapes, sizes, positions, distances, and spatial relationships.
Statistics concerns collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting data.
Mathematical logic studies valid reasoning and formal statements.
